### Building a New Desktop PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide Below you’ll find everything from choosing parts to installing your operating system. I’ve broken it into three phases: | Phase | What You Need | |-------|---------------| | **Planning** | Budget, purpose, component compatibility | | **Assembly** | Parts, tools, workspace | | **Post‑Build** | Software, drivers, tweaks | --- #### 1️⃣ Planning & Component Selection *(Spend ~30–60 min researching before buying anything)* | Category | Key Questions | Typical Choices | |----------|-----------------|------------------| | **CPU** | • Do you need multi‑core performance?
• Will you overclock? | AMD Ryzen 5/7 / Intel Core i5/i7 | | **Motherboard** | • Which socket matches CPU?
• How many PCIe slots, RAM slots, M.2 drives?
• Does it support Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth if desired? | B550/M570 (AMD) or Z590/Z690 (Intel) | | **RAM** | • Minimum 16 GB for gaming; 32+ for content creation.
• DDR4 vs DDR5 depends on motherboard.| 3200 MHz DDR4 or 6000 MHz DDR5 | | **GPU** | • Target resolution/frame rate?
• Power supply headroom? | RTX 3060/3070/4070 or Radeon RX 6700 XT etc. | | **Storage** | • SSD NVMe for boot + games/apps.
• HDD for bulk storage? | 500 GB NVMe + optional 2TB SATA HDD | | **PSU** | • Wattage ≥ GPU + CPU + peripherals + margin (~20%).
• Modular cables help cable mgmt. | 650W Gold modular PSU | | **Case** | • Size fits motherboard (ATX, mATX).
• Airflow, noise level, aesthetics. | Mid‑tower ATX case with good airflow | | **Cooling** | • Stock cooler may suffice; aftermarket improves temps/noise. | Aftermarket air cooler or all‑in‑one liquid cooler | | **Peripherals** | Monitor, keyboard, mouse, speakers/headset. | Depends on use-case | *Tip:* Use online “PC Part Picker” sites (pcpartpicker.com, Newegg’s Build Planner) to check compatibility automatically. --- #### 2️⃣ Assembly Checklist (Assume you have an anti‑static wrist strap—recommended!) ##### 🔧 Tools Needed - Phillips #2 screwdriver - Anti‑static mat/wristband - Thermal paste (if not pre‑applied on cooler) ##### 📦 Workspace Setup - Clean, flat surface. - Keep screws organized (use small containers per part type). ##### 🛠️ Step‑By‑Step Instructions | Step | Action | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **A. Prepare Case** | Remove side panels. Locate standoffs for motherboard mounting. | Some cases come pre‑stuck; others require manual placement. | | **B. Install Motherboard** | Place motherboard onto standoff grid. Secure with screws. | Align rear I/O shield first. | | **C. Mount CPU** | Lift CPU socket lever → open slot → align pin pattern → gently place CPU → lower lever. | Avoid touching pins. | | **D. Apply Thermal Paste** | If cooler doesn’t have pre‑paste, apply pea‑size amount at center. | Too much paste spreads unevenly. | | **E. Attach Cooler** | For air coolers: screw fan bracket then mount heatsink.
For AIOs: attach pump block, connect radiator fans later. | Ensure proper orientation of fans (intake/outlet). | | **F. Insert RAM** | Snap sticks into DIMM slots until clicks lock. | Verify correct slot order (often color‑coded). | | **G. Add Storage Drives** | Mount NVMe SSD in M.2 slot; secure with screw.
Mount SATA drive(s) in bay, connect data + power cables. | Check whether M.2 uses PCIe x4 lanes. | | **H. Install PSU** | Slide PSU into bottom tray, orient fan toward intake/exhaust as specified. Connect main 24‑pin + EPS12V to motherboard. | Route cables neatly using ties. | | **I. Mount Graphics Card** | Remove appropriate expansion slot covers. Insert card into top PCIe x16 slot. Screw to case. | Connect required PCIe power connectors. | | **J. Cable Management** | Tidy up remaining cables: SATA, USB headers, front panel connectors. | Good airflow keeps temperatures down. | | **K. Front Panel Connections** | Hook up power button, reset switch, LEDs, audio jack, USB ports according to motherboard manual. | Double‑check each header alignment. | | **L. Final Checks** | Confirm all connections, ensure no loose screws, verify cooling fans spin when powered. | Turn off power while checking. | | **M. First Boot** | Plug in monitor, keyboard, mouse. Switch on PSU. Enter BIOS via `Del`/`F2`. | Set boot priority to UEFI mode, enable XMP profile for RAM. | | **N. Install Operating System** | Create bootable USB (Windows 10/11 ISO or Ubuntu). Boot from USB, follow installer prompts. | Format primary partition during install. | | **O. Driver Installation** | Once OS boots, download latest chipset, graphics, network drivers from manufacturer websites. | Windows Update often pulls most drivers automatically. | | **P. Benchmark & Test** | Run stress tests (`Prime95`, `Unigine Heaven`) to confirm stability. | Monitor temperatures under load (<70°C for GPUs, <80°C for CPUs). | --- #### 3️⃣ Post‑Build Tweaks & Maintenance | Item | Why It Matters | Quick Fixes | |------|----------------|-------------| | **BIOS Updates** | Improves hardware compatibility, fixes bugs. | Download latest firmware from motherboard site. | | **Fan Curves** | Balance noise vs cooling. | Adjust in BIOS or software utilities (MSI Dragon Center, ASUS AI Suite). | | **Cable Routing** | Enhances airflow, reduces dust accumulation. | Re‑route after initial test runs. | | **Dust Filters** | Keeps internals clean. | Replace filters quarterly. | | **Regular Backups** | Protect against accidental loss. | Use cloud services or external hard drives. | --- #### 🎯 Common Pitfalls & Tips | Issue | Prevention | |-------|------------| | *Short circuits due to misplaced screws.* | Never touch metal contacts inside the case unless grounded. | | *Overheating early on.* | Make sure thermal paste isn’t too thick; keep case vents unobstructed. | | *Boot failure (“No video detected”).* | Check GPU seating, power connector, and that the display input matches the port used. | | *Driver conflicts causing crashes.* | Uninstall old drivers before installing new ones; let Windows update handle basic drivers initially. | | *Noise spikes.* | Inspect fan bearings; replace noisy fans. | --- #### 🚀 Ready to Start? If you’re still unsure which exact models fit best, feel free to share: - Your budget range ($300–$2000+) - Primary use (gaming, streaming, editing, everyday tasks) - Any brand preferences or constraints With those details, I can suggest a tailored bill of materials and even walk through the build step‑by‑step!

The user asks "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions or guidance. We can provide steps and considerations.

We might also ask clarifying questions about budget, usage (gaming, office), but we could give general guide. Provide components list, assembly process, tips. Also mention safety precautions, cable management, BIOS setup, OS installation. Possibly link to resources like Tom's Hardware guides. No need to call tool because no recipe needed. So just answer with detailed explanation.
